high.title: After Weaker Inflation, Economists Revise 2026 Estimates; Check This Monday's Focus Report (13)
high.summary:
The Banco Central do Brasil released its latest weekly Focus Report on Monday, showing that inflation expectations declined for the second consecutive week — a meaningful positive signal for BRL and fixed income markets. The market consensus for 2026 IPCA dropped from 5.30% to 5.16%, reflecting the more benign official inflation print released on Friday, July 10th. Expectations for 2027 edged marginally higher to 4.20% from 4.18%, while 2028 and 2029 remain anchored at 3.70% and 3.50%, respectively. The back-end of the curve holding steady is a constructive sign for long-duration Brazilian government bonds. For FX and rates traders, the consecutive downward revisions to near-term inflation reduce pressure on the BCB to maintain an overly restrictive policy stance, supporting expectations for continued monetary easing. This increases the attractiveness of Brazilian fixed income on a carry-adjusted basis and provides a near-term tailwind for BRL stability. Watch for whether the next IPCA print confirms this disinflationary trend, which would further solidify BCB's easing trajectory.

---

high.title: Escalation of War and Rising Oil Prices Pressure Markets; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Rises Today (July 13)
high.summary: Markets are opening the week on a cautious footing as Middle East tensions escalate sharply following a direct military exchange between the United States and Iran over the weekend. President Trump authorized airstrikes against Iranian targets, framed by Washington as a response to an Iranian attack on a commercial vessel in the region. Iran retaliated, triggering a broad risk-off environment globally.

medium.title: Musical Chairs: BofA Assesses Which Stocks May Enter and Exit the Ibovespa in the First Preliminary Review
medium.summary:
Bank of America has published a preliminary estimate ahead of the first Ibovespa rebalancing preview, due to be released on August 3rd. According to BofA, Tenda (TEND3) and Itaú's ordinary shares (ITUB3) are candidates to join the index, while PetroReconcavo (RECV3) may be dropped from the next composition. For international fund managers with Brazilian equity exposure, index rebalancing events carry meaningful flow implications — stocks added to the Ibovespa typically attract passive and index-tracking inflows, while those removed face selling pressure. The potential inclusion of Itaú ordinary shares (ITUB3) is particularly noteworthy given the bank's systemic weight in Brazil's financial sector and its sensitivity to Selic rate dynamics. Traders should monitor the official August 3rd preview for confirmation and begin positioning accordingly in affected names.

---

medium.title: CSN Mineração (CMIN3) Jumps 21% and MRV (MRVE3) Posts Worst Weekly Performance on Ibovespa; Weekly Index Highlights
medium.summary: The Ibovespa posted its third consecutive week of gains, rising 2.18% to close at 177,866.37 points, driven by optimism around a potential US-Iran peace agreement in the Middle East and growing market bets on a continuation of the BCB's monetary easing cycle. The spot USD/BRL rate fell 1.17% on the week, closing at R$5.1084, reflecting improved risk appetite and a softer dollar environment. CSN Mineração (CMIN3) was the standout performer with a 21% weekly surge, while MRV (MRVE3) was the worst performer. The combination of geopolitical de-escalation hopes and dovish BCB expectations is providing a constructive backdrop for both Brazilian equities and the Real — fund managers should monitor whether Middle East tensions re-escalate, as this could quickly reverse recent FX and equity gains.

medium.title: Trump Contradicts Evidence, Claims Falling Inflation and Oil Prices
medium.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed on Truth Social that prices in the US are falling alongside oil and gas prices, contradicting official data showing US CPI at 4.2% year-on-year in May, up from 3.8% in April, with the PCE deflator also trending higher. While this is primarily a US domestic political story, it carries indirect relevance for Brazilian markets: persistent US inflation limits the Federal Reserve's ability to cut rates, keeping the USD broadly supported and maintaining pressure on EM currencies including the BRL. A higher-for-longer Fed stance would narrow the interest rate differential attractiveness of Brazilian assets and could cap BRL appreciation. Traders should watch upcoming US inflation data closely as a key external driver for USD/BRL direction.
